findings.title: Breaking API change: `amount` removed from the response, and the in-repo web client is not updated
findings.explanation: The web client reads `invoice.amount` (web/src/api/invoices.ts:4 and web/src/components/InvoiceRow.tsx:10). After this change `amount` is undefined, so `invoice.amount / 100` evaluates to NaN and the invoice list shows NaN. Any external API consumers will break in the same way. Update the web types and components in the same PR. For rolling deploys and external clients, emit both `amount` and `amount_cents` for a deprecation period, then remove `amount` later. Alternatively, version the API. Also check for API docs, an OpenAPI spec and tests that reference `amount`.

findings.title: Input row field and the other API surface still use the ambiguous name `amount`
findings.explanation: The `InvoiceRow.amount` field and the DB column are still called `amount`, so the naming is inconsistent. The `/payments` route also uses `amount`, and it has the same ambiguity. This is acceptable for a response-only rename. Consider noting the follow-up, or renaming the other surfaces consistently. Also consider documenting the unit in the response type.

findings.title: Number() on BIGINT can lose precision
findings.explanation: This is pre-existing. `Number(row.amount)` loses precision above 2^53 cents. That is unrealistic for invoices, so it is only worth a comment.

## Rename invoice amount to amount_cents

`amount` is ambiguous: people reading the API assume dollars. This renames the response field to `amount_cents` so the unit is explicit.

   return {
     id: row.id,
-    amount: Number(row.amount),

     currency: row.currency,
     status: row.status,
     period_start: row.period_start.toISOString(),
